title: GDP — third estimate, Q3 2026 (with Industries, Corporate Profits, State GDP and State Personal Income)
source: EST: bea.gov/news/schedule, fetched direct 2026-09-05, whose December 2026 block reads "December 23, 8:30 AM — GDP (Third Estimate), Industries, Corporate Profits, State GDP, and State Personal Income, 3rd Quarter 2026" (the same page's November block reads "November 25, 8:30 AM — GDP (Second Estimate) and Corporate Profits, 3rd Quarter 2026"). Primary-sourced, and filed estimate on the one count that always applies here: this lane may not self-confirm an event it discovered in-sweep — the confirming re-read of the same BEA schedule page belongs to whichever lane owns this event's own never-assessed research. Corroborated by pattern: the identical Q2 vintage (gdp-q2-2026-third-2026-09-30) sits on this calendar as BEA-confirmed with the same payload bundle
notes: The final Q3 vintage, and it lands FOURTEEN DAYS AFTER the 12-08/09 FOMC — which is the whole reason it is worth tracking: it is the release that proves whether the December dots were set on a number BEA subsequently moved. Discovered during the gdp-q3-2026-second-2026-11-25 initial research (2026-09-05), where it is the load-bearing fact behind that event's "last vintage the committee sees" framing; the ledger there measures the second estimate's revision channel, and this print is where any second-round revision to the same quarter shows up. Shares its 08:30 ET slot with November PCE (pce-2026-12-23) and with durable goods (durable-goods-2026-12-23), and sits in the same holiday-thinned week as the 12-24 1:00pm ET NYSE half session and the 12-25 close (NYSE primary, fetched 2026-09-05) — the same minimum-liquidity structure the 11-25 pair carries, one month later. Impact `medium` matches gdp-q2-2026-third-2026-09-30: a third estimate is the least market-moving GDP vintage by construction, but it carries the annual corporate-profits and industry detail nothing else publishes. Funding is the one live risk: H.R. 6500 runs only to 2026-12-11 (cr-expiry-2026-12-11), twelve days BEFORE this date, and BEA deletes rather than delays a GDP vintage in a lapse — so unlike the 11-25 second estimate, this release sits on the far side of the cliff and inherits the existence risk the 10-29 advance estimate shed.
